extra.message: User-controlled input 'username' from the query parameter is concatenated directly into a Jinja2 template string via Jinja2.from_string('Welcome ' + username + '!').render(). An attacker can inject Jinja2 template directives (e.g., {{7*7}}) or leverage Jinja2's object hierarchy to achieve remote code execution (e.g., {{''.__class__.__mro__[1].__subclasses__()}}). This is a classic Server-Side Template Injection vulnerability.

Jinja2 Environment is created without autoescape=True (line 11: Jinja2 = Environment()). Combined with returning the rendered output as HTMLResponse (line 19), this means any user input rendered via {{ }} in templates will not be HTML-escaped, enabling Cross-Site Scripting. Even the commented-out 'safe' implementation on line 17 would be vulnerable to XSS without autoescaping enabled.
